leads.summary: The requested package does not actually scope mise which's executable search
leads.consequence: Conditional on another configured and installed tool exposing the same executable, the wrapper can execute that other tool. For example, a Node installation with a globally installed `pi` before Omarchy's `pi` tool in mise's toolset can satisfy `mise which --tool pi pi` first. Merely passing --tool pi does not restrict which to pi. This matters to the default pi launcher and to custom launchers with colliding bin names; the new tests use a mock which unconditionally reports the expected path and miss it.
leads.triage: behavioural -> Opus follow-up 1 confirmed (sealed run plan-which1, corrected by plan-which2); published as N1

leads.summary: Exact-template migration leaves generated, shell-escaped wrappers in their old form
leads.consequence: A user who previously ran omarchy-mise-install for a package or bin containing $, backticks, double quotes, backslashes, ! or control characters gets a %q-escaped old wrapper. The migration recognizes only the double-quoted form, silently leaves that actual generator output untouched and then its completion marker prevents retry. The affected command retains the old bare-name resolution and possible recursion. Ordinary bundled package specs, including scoped npm and bracketed Muse, do use the double-quoted form.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (q1-q6, %q-escaped names unmatched); published as one boundary sentence (no call site produces them)

leads.summary: Related open PR #8692 has mutually exclusive generator and test expectations
leads.consequence: If both PRs merge without reconciling the implementations and tests, a last-writer-wins resolution fails one PR's tests: #8692 uses `mise bin-paths` and checks `candidate=...`, whereas this PR uses `mise which --tool` and checks the which call and bin_path template. Both also add a migration for the same prior wrapper form, with different template detection/ordering. The merge has textual conflicts in shared files. This is an integration alert, not a claim that either approach automatically breaks production when consciously reconciled.
leads.triage: factual; coordinator verified #8692 open, same files, bin-paths approach, same-shape migration via read-only gh; published as context in N1 suggested change

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on `b0ebcec`, reassessing the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13090#issuecomment-5826080291) after the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13090#issuecomment-5833494078).

**Verified:** the new migration upgrades existing wrappers, and both previously failing tests pass. One newly found, narrow behavior difference in the `mise which --tool` lookup (present since `c8a7f2c`) is described below. It also qualifies the earlier project-pin point.

| Earlier point | Status at `b0ebcec` |
|---|---|
| Existing wrappers keep the looping exec line | **Resolved** by `migrations/1790343618.sh` |
| Two shell tests assert the old exec line | **Resolved** |
| Uninstalled project-pinned version stops the wrapper | **Still present**, accepted by the author. Now reaches existing installs too; see the qualification below |
| Optional loop-guard test for `mise-install-test.sh` | Unchanged, still optional |
| Hermes CLI wrapper uses the same bare-name exec | **Resolved upstream** by #12844 (merged into `quattro` after the earlier review), which retires the mise-backed Hermes wrapper through `migrations/1790017600.sh` |

**Verified** in isolated runs with the real generator and a logging stub `mise`:

- For every `install/user/mise.sh` call site, including the Muse `http:` package, a wrapper written by the previous generator was regenerated byte-identical to what `omarchy-mise-install` writes today. Scoped npm names, `@version` suffixes, a bin name that differs from the command name, and names with spaces or `;&|*?[]'~#%=,` also round-trip, with every argument reaching `mise` intact. Names the generator escapes (containing `$`, backticks, quotes, backslashes or `!`) are left unmigrated; no Omarchy call site uses them.
- Wrappers from every generator version `quattro` shipped end in the current form after `1784909971`, `1787573629` and `1790343618` run in order.
- The migration leaves alone:
  - wrappers with an added line;
  - symlinks, FIFOs, directories, unreadable files and large binaries;
  - unrelated scripts;
  - wrappers already in the new form (not rewritten).
- A missing, empty or symlinked `~/.local/bin` exits 0. The migration makes no `mise` calls, so offline updates are unaffected.
- `mise-wrapper-quiet-migration-test.sh` and `default-agent-test.sh` fail at `c8a7f2c` and pass at `b0ebcec`, and `default-agent-test.sh` runs all 48 checks again. The new `mise-wrapper-resolution-migration-test.sh` passes, and fails when the generator is swapped back to the base version.
- With current `quattro` merged in, all four wrapper tests pass.

### `mise which --tool <pkg>` can return another tool's executable

Without a version, `--tool <pkg>` does not limit the lookup to `<pkg>`. `mise which` returns the first installed, active mise tool that ships `<bin>`, in mise's own order: project config first, then global config in file order. The old `mise x <pkg> -- <bin>` put `<pkg>`'s bin directory first among the directories mise adds to PATH. This is from mise 2026.9.12 source (`src/cli/which.rs` 108-117, `src/toolset/builder.rs` 293-326, `src/toolset/mod.rs` 694-711).

Packaged mise 2026.9.4, offline, with synthetic `npm:` tools `toola` and `toolb` that both ship `shared`. The wrapper was generated for `npm:toolb shared` and run by absolute path:

```text
situation                                          base wrapper     head wrapper
global config lists toola before toolb             runs toolb       runs toola
global has toolb, project mise.toml adds toola     runs toolb       runs toola
toolb listed first (control)                       runs toolb       runs toolb
project pins toolb to an uninstalled version       (installs pin)   (installs pin), then execs toola's path
```

`mise which --tool npm:toolb onlya` even returned toola's `onlya`, a name toolb does not ship. Running the wrapper's `mise use -g` did not move its package ahead of toola. In the pin row, `mise which` returned toola's path with exit 0; both wrappers then started installing the pin in `mise x` (offline, so the final exec of toola's path is inferred from source).

**Impact:** a wrapper can silently run a different install of the same CLI (for example `npm:@anthropic-ai/claude-code` next to Omarchy's `claude`), or an unrelated program with the same name (the registry `cf` is the Cloud Foundry CLI, while Omarchy's `cf` wrapper is the Cloudflare CLI). The last row qualifies the earlier project-pin point: the wrapper exits with `is not installed` only when no other active tool ships the name; otherwise it goes on to install the pin and then runs the other tool's binary. Exposure is low. Omarchy's own tools do not overlap, and Omarchy puts mise's shims ahead of `~/.local/bin`, so the wrapper is reached mainly in #13040-style contexts or by direct path.

**Suggested change:** either accept and document this lookup order, or resolve the binary only within `<pkg>`. `mise bin-paths <pkg>` keeps only the requested tool (`src/cli/bin_paths.rs` 30-39). In the same run it printed only toolb's directory. For the uninstalled pin it printed nothing and exited 0, so a wrapper would need to treat empty output as failure. Open PR #8692 proposes this approach for the same loop (`mise bin-paths` plus an `-x` check) and adds a migration that matches the same previous wrapper form. The two PRs change the same generator line and the same test assertions.

**Optional test improvement:** in `mise-wrapper-resolution-migration-test.sh`, removing the migration's symlink guard or dropping the third argument to `omarchy-mise-install` still passes. The test's only symlink points at an already-migrated wrapper, and every case has the same bin and command name. A stale wrapper whose bin differs from its command name (like `mise-exec-era` in the quiet-migration test) and a symlink to a stale wrapper outside `~/.local/bin` would catch both.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Head `b0ebcec` against the earlier head `c8a7f2c` and base `28ceaae`, plus `b0ebcec` with current `quattro` merged. The migration was run across 29 wrapper shapes, the generator versions `quattro` shipped, and filesystem edge cases, and the wrapper tests at each revision where they exist, with mutations of the new migration, all in isolation with no network. The lookup comparison used packaged mise 2026.9.4 with synthetic `npm:` tools; the relevant mise 2026.9.12 source was compared and has no lookup change. Other backends and the #13040 PATH layout combined with a collision were not run. In the project-pin case the install was only started offline; its completion and the following exec are inferred from mise source. No real user wrappers, no network installs, no desktop session.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
